findings.rationale: NY's uploaded updates are near zero in a large share of rounds (update norm exactly 0 in rounds 1, 8, 13, 17, 19; many other rounds below 0.25x median), while normal rounds show norms of about 1x median. The median norm ratio across 20 rounds is 0.0054 (size-adjusted z = -12.9). This is the signature of uploading the global model back without training. Its local performance (AUC 0.85, CITL near 0) looks normal, so this is not label noise.

CT's updates are exactly zero in several rounds (4, 5, 6, 7, 11, 16, 17) and near zero in others, while its remaining rounds are at normal scale (about 1x median). Its median norm ratio is 0.0081 (z = -10.4) and its minimum is 0. This fits the free-rider pattern of returning the global model unchanged in some rounds. Local AUC (0.81) and CITL (0.003) are normal.

NJ's updates are exactly zero in rounds 4, 5, 7, 8, 17 and near zero in several other rounds, with normal-scale updates in the rest. Its median norm ratio is 0.0044 (z = -7.0) and its minimum norm ratio is also far below the federation (z = -6.3). This is consistent with intermittent free-riding. Local performance (AUC 0.78) is not anomalous.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income). The clearest signal is three clients (NY, CT, NJ) whose uploaded updates are exactly or nearly zero in a substantial share of rounds, which matches free-riding. Their local performance and calibration look normal, so they are not label-noise or prevalence faults. Other outliers (MD and WI/DC/MO/WV subgroup O/E values driven by near-zero predictions, ND HighChol sd, NC GenHlth p99, DC/RI/TN feature tails, NV/VI/NC/NM drift entries) did not hold up on narrower re-checks (ND HighChol and NC GenHlth returned normal values at higher epsilon), so they are treated as noise. WA's large norm ratio is consistent with its size. Budget used: 19.5 of 20. Final decision rests on the update-norm evidence for the three free-riders.
